tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has collected a Qwen long-horizon agent report, an O-RAN benchmark, and four Oct 20-22 arXiv papers on training tool-using and search agents.
whats_new: Oct 23: AWS publishes a hands-on guide to multi-turn RL on Amazon SageMaker AI, training on whole-task outcomes with a Wordle example.
why_it_matters: The SageMaker guide is the first managed-platform recipe in the thread, so teams on AWS can try outcome-based multi-turn RL without building the training harness. The arXiv papers cover rollout cost, stateful environments, search-state awareness and per-decision credit assignment; QwenGyre (a secondary-source report) and X-RIC remain research or telecom-specific.

status.detail: A loose set of agentic-RL items; the newest moves from papers to a managed-platform guide.

beats.headline: Alibaba Qwen introduces QwenGyre for elastic RL on extra-long-horizon agents
beats.summary: Reported via MarkTechPost; targets agent tasks that run far longer than standard RL rollouts.

beats.headline: X-RIC benchmarks agentic RAN controllers for reinforcement learning
beats.summary: Targets O-RAN controllers rather than LLM post-training.

beats.headline: Agentic RL papers: rollout budgets, stateful environments, search-state awareness, credit assignment
beats.summary: Four arXiv papers on cutting rollout cost, extending RL beyond tool-centric settings, teaching search agents to assess their own state, and crediting individual decisions within an episode.

beats.headline: AWS walks through multi-turn RL on SageMaker AI
beats.summary: A hands-on pipeline that trains on the outcome of a whole multi-step task, demonstrated on Wordle.

open_questions: Does calibrated rollout budgeting cut MCP-agent training cost on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does BIRD-RL's gain on small language models hold on larger models?
Does Qwen publish QwenGyre weights, code, or benchmarks that show the elastic RL gain on long-horizon agent tasks?
Does the SageMaker MTRL recipe carry from Wordle to tool-using agent tasks, and at what training cost?
Does twin-world credit assignment improve agent training on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
take_for_builders: If you train tool-using models, read the rollout-budget and twin-world credit-assignment papers for cheaper, finer-grained learning signal; if you run on AWS, try the SageMaker Wordle pipeline before planning around it, and wait for Qwen's primary QwenGyre release.
